greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ καιρῷ ἐκείνῳ κατέβη Ιουδας ἀπὸ τῶν ἀδελφῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀφίκετο ἕως πρὸς ἄνθρωπόν τινα Οδολλαμίτην, ᾧ ὄνομα Ιρας.
hint: Judah leaves his brothers and goes down to an Adullamite named Hirah.

notes.text: καιρός is the right or proper time, the due measure: here, at that time, joining the story to the sale of Joseph just told.
ἀφικνέομαι, to arrive, with ἕως before a preposition: as far as to a certain man.

names.gloss: (Ιουδας, from Hebrew Yĕhûdâ, which the Hebrew of 29:35 hears in yādâ, "to praise")
(Οδολλαμίτης, from Hebrew ʿĂdullāmî, a man of Adullam, of uncertain meaning)
(Ιρας, from Hebrew Ḥîrâ, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ εἶδεν ἐκεῖ Ιουδας θυγατέρα ἀνθρώπου Χαναναίου, ᾗ ὄνομα Σαυα, καὶ ἔλαβεν αὐτὴν καὶ εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτήν.
hint: Judah sees the daughter of a Canaanite, named Shua, and takes her.

notes.text: ᾗ is feminine: Shua is the daughter's name. The Hebrew has bat-ʾîš kĕnaʿănî ûšĕmô šûaʿ, the daughter of a Canaanite man whose name was Shua — the father's name; 12 calls her bat-šûaʿ, Shua's daughter.
He went in to her, the idiom of 16:2, 29:23 and 30:4.

names.gloss: (Σαυα, from Hebrew Šûaʿ, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ συλλαβοῦσα ἔτεκεν υἱὸν καὶ ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ηρ.
hint: She bears a son, Er.

notes.text: No new subject: the one who conceived and bore names him. The Hebrew has he called for Er, and she for Onan and Shelah; the Greek has the mother name all three.
συλλαμβάνω, to gather together and take hold of, and so to conceive.

names.gloss: (Ηρ, from Hebrew ʿĒr, usually connected with ʿûr, "to be awake")

greek: καὶ συλλαβοῦσα ἔτι ἔτεκεν υἱὸν καὶ ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Αυναν.
hint: She bears a second son, Onan.

notes.text: yet, again: a second birth.

reading: and [[having collected|having collected, having gathered together, having taken up, having laid hold of and seized, having comprehended, having conceived|συλλαμβάνω]] [[yet|yet, as yet, still, further, besides, moreover|ἔτι]] [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, produced|τίκτω]] a son and [[called|called, summoned, called to herself, invited|καλέω]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of him [[name:Αυναν]].

names.gloss: (Αυναν, from Hebrew ʾÔnān, usually connected with ʾôn, "vigour")

greek: καὶ προσθεῖσα ἔτι ἔτεκεν υἱὸν καὶ ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Σηλωμ. αὐτὴ δὲ ἦν ἐν Χασβι, ἡνίκα ἔτεκεν αὐτούς.
hint: A third son, Shelah, born at Chezib.

notes.text: προστίθημι with another verb, she added and bore: the Hebrew idiom for doing a thing again.
She was in Chasbi when she bore them. The Hebrew has wĕhāyâ bikzîb, and he was at Chezib, when she bore him: Judah, and Shelah only.

(Χασβι, from Hebrew Kĕzîb, usually connected with kāzab, "to lie, deceive")

greek: καὶ ἔλαβεν Ιουδας γυναῖκα Ηρ τῷ πρωτοτόκῳ αὐτοῦ, ᾗ ὄνομα Θαμαρ.
hint: Judah takes Tamar as wife for Er, his first-born.

notes.text: A woman for Er: the dative of the one she is taken for, with τῷ πρωτοτόκῳ in apposition.

reading: and [[took|took, received, took hold of and grasped and seized|λαμβάνω]] [[name:Ιουδας]] [[woman|woman, mistress and lady, wife and spouse, mortal woman|γυνή]] to [[name:Ηρ]] to the first-born of him, to which [[a name|a name, fame, a mere name, a phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] [[name:Θαμαρ]].

greek: ἐγένετο δὲ Ηρ πρωτότοκος Ιουδα πονηρὸς ἐναντίον κυρίου, καὶ ἀπέκτεινεν αὐτὸν ὁ θεός.
hint: Er is wicked before the Lord, and God kills him.

notes.text: κύριος without the article for the one before whom Er is evil, and ὁ θεός for the one who kills him, as the Hebrew has the one name, YHWH, twice.
γίνομαι with a predicate: he came to be wicked.

reading: [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ηρ]] first-born of [[name:Ιουδα]] [[toilsome|toilsome, painful, grievous, good-for-nothing, bad and worthless, wicked|πονηρός]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] [[of lord|of lord, of master, of the one having power and authority over|κύριος]], and [[killed|killed, slew, condemned to death|ἀποκτείνω]] him [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]].

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Ιουδας τῷ Αυναν Εἴσελθε πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου καὶ γάμβρευσαι αὐτὴν καὶ ἀνάστησον σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου.
hint: Judah tells Onan to go in to his brother's wife and raise up seed for him.

notes.text: Aorist middle imperative of γαμβρεύω, which LSJ gives as to form connexions by marriage, and in the middle to marry, citing this verse. Middle Liddell lacks it. The Hebrew yabbēm is the levirate duty of a husband's brother.
ἀνίστημι in the first aorist is causal, to make stand up, raise up: raise up seed for your brother.

greek: γνοὺς δὲ Αυναν ὅτι οὐκ αὐτῷ ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα, ἐγίνετο ὅταν εἰσήρχετο πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ, ἐξέχεεν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τοῦ μὴ δοῦναι σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ.
hint: Onan, knowing the seed would not be his, spills it on the ground whenever he goes in to her.

notes.text: Imperfects: it would happen whenever he went in — a repeated act, not once.
Aorist of ἐκχέω, to pour out, set after the imperfects: each time, he poured it out.
The genitive articular infinitive with μή, of purpose: so as not to give seed to his brother.

hint: What he did is evil before God, and God kills him too.

hint: Judah sends Tamar to her father's house to wait as a widow until Shelah is grown, fearing for him.

εἶπεν, said, for what he said to himself: lest he too die.
Imperfect: she was staying there, for the time the next verse passes over.

hint: Shua dies; after mourning, Judah goes up to the shearers at Timnah with Hirah.

notes.text: The days were multiplied: time passed.
Aorist passive participle of παρακαλέω, to call to one's side, exhort, comfort: having been comforted, after the mourning.

hint: Tamar is told that her father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.

notes.text: A plural participle with no subject named: people told her, saying.

greek: καὶ περιελομένη τὰ ἱμάτια τῆς χηρεύσεως ἀφʼ ἑαυτῆς περιεβάλετο θέριστρον καὶ ἐκαλλωπίσατο καὶ ἐκάθισεν πρὸς ταῖς πύλαις Αιναν, ἥ ἐστιν ἐν παρόδῳ Θαμνα· εἶδεν γὰρ ὅτι μέγας γέγονεν Σηλωμ, αὐτὸς δὲ οὐκ ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν αὐτῷ γυναῖκα.
hint: Tamar puts off her widow's clothes, veils herself and sits at the gates of Enaim on the way to Timnah.

notes.text: χήρευσις, widowhood: the garments that marked it. LSJ glosses it only by χηρεία, widowhood, and cites this verse.
a light summer garment, Middle Liddell's one sense; the Hebrew ṣāʿîp is a veil.
At the gates of Ainan. The Hebrew petaḥ ʿênayim is the opening of Enaim, or of two springs; the Greek makes Αιναν a place with gates.

notes.lemma: αὐτὸς δὲ οὐκ ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν αὐτῷ γυναῖκα
notes.text: Active, with Judah as subject: he did not give her to him as wife. The Hebrew is passive, and she had not been given to him.

greek: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὴν Ιουδας ἔδοξεν αὐτὴν πόρνην εἶναι· κατεκαλύψατο γὰρ τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτῆς, καὶ οὐκ ἐπέγνω αὐτήν.
hint: Judah sees her and takes her for a harlot, since her face is covered.

notes.text: Why was the fence broken through because of you? φραγμός, a fencing in, a barrier. The Hebrew has mah-pāraṣtā ʿāleykā pāreṣ, what a breach you have made for yourself, and Perez is named for the breach, pereṣ; the Greek's φραγμός keeps the barrier, not the name.
καί after a clause with ὡς, opening the main clause: the Hebrew way of joining them.

reading: [[as|as, according as, considering, like|ὡς]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[collected and brought to|collected and brought to, gathered together|ἐπισυνάγω]] [[the hand|the hand, the hand and arm, the arm|χείρ]], and [[straightway|straightway, forthwith, at once, just, directly and simply|εὐθύς]] [[went out of|went out of, came out, went away and marched off, went forth|ἐξέρχομαι]] [[the son of the same mother|the son of the same mother, the brother, the near kinsman|ἀδελφός]] of him. the one [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] what [[was cut in two|was cut in two, was cut through, was broken through|διακόπτω]] [[through|through, throughout and over, during, by aid of and by means of, by reason of, because of, for the sake of|διά + accusative]] you [[a fencing in|a fencing in, a blocking up, a fence, a paling, a palisade, a place fenced off, an enclosure, a partition|φραγμός]]? and [[called|called, summoned, called to herself, invited|καλέω]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of him [[name:Φαρες]].

greek: καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο ἐξῆλθεν ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ, ἐφʼ ᾧ ἦν ἐπὶ τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ τὸ κόκκινον· καὶ ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ζαρα.
hint: The brother with the scarlet on his hand comes out next, and is named Zerah.

notes.text: ἐπί with the dative, on whom, upon whose hand was the scarlet.
The Hebrew Zeraḥ is heard as a rising, a shining, of the scarlet; the Greek gives the name without its play.

reading: and [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[went out of|went out of, came out, went away and marched off, went forth|ἐξέρχομαι]] [[the son of the same mother|the son of the same mother, the brother, the near kinsman|ἀδελφός]] of him, [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + dative]] to which was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + dative]] [[to the hand|to the hand, to the hand and arm, to the arm|χείρ]] of him the scarlet; and [[called|called, summoned, called to herself, invited|καλέω]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of him [[name:Ζαρα]].

names.gloss: (Ζαρα, from Hebrew Zeraḥ, usually connected with zāraḥ, "to rise, shine")
